notes.claim: With algebra tiles, matching tiles on both sides of x + 7 = 3x + 1 can be removed, which is the same as taking the same amount off both sides.
Oak National Academy teaches that equations with unknowns on both sides can be manipulated so the unknowns end up on one side.
A formula remains balanced if the same operation is performed on both sides, which is why matching terms can come off both sides.

sources.title: 2.11 Rearranging formulas 2
sources.quote: A formula remains balanced if we perform the same operation to both sides of it.

sources.title: Mastery materials writing frame
sources.quote: For example, when solving the equation x + 7 = 3 x + 1, there is one +1 tile and one + x tile on both sides that can be removed.

sources.title: Solving linear equations KS3 | Y8 Maths | Lesson Resources | Oak National Academy
sources.quote: I can recognise that equations with unknowns on both sides of the equation can be manipulated so that the unknowns are on one side and then solve this equation.
